# Decisions

All made by Simon Haegler in the planning project, 2026-11-21. Re-open only with him.

| # | Decision | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| D1 | Architecture **option A**: OpenUSD v26.08 in WASM including Hydra (hf, hd, hdar, hdsi, hio, pxOsd, cameraUtil, geomUtil) and usdImaging. Reprojection in a C++ `HdSingleInputFilteringSceneIndex` after `UsdImagingStageSceneIndex`. A C++ `HdSceneIndexObserver` + embind feeds a minimal WebGL2 mesh pass in a Maps SDK `RenderNode`. | Option B (placement in JS) dropped. Option D (offline Python + pyproj) kept as ground truth. hdar and hio added 2026-11-21: usdImaging links both (both GPU-free). |
| D2 | **No three.js, no Needle**, no web render delegate. | |
| D3 | Implement the geospatial CRS proposal ([Tamrat-B/OpenUSD-proposals#1](https://github.com/Tamrat-B/OpenUSD-proposals/pull/1), pinned at 4120379f) in C++ on v26.08: `GeospatialCRS` (`uniform token crs:wkt`; see D14), `GeospatialCRSBindingAPI` (`double3 crs:position`, `double3 crs:orientation`). | Pin the proposal commit; keep property names in one tokens file. |
| D4 | **Engine plugins.** `usdGeospatial` defines `UsdGeospatialCoordinateOperationEngine` + `UsdGeospatialEngineRegistry` (PlugRegistry discovery; selection by `USDGEOSPATIAL_ENGINE` env setting, API call, or plugInfo priority). Core has no PROJ dependency. | |
| D5 | **PROJ first**, everywhere including the browser (PROJ + SQLite built from source with emscripten, trimmed `proj.db`, no curl/libtiff, no grids in browser). One pinned PROJ version for native and WASM. | Esri Projection Engine (`usdGeospatialEsriPE`, JS bridge to `projectOperator`) is follow-on milestone E1. |
| D6 | Branch `geospatial-web` on mistafunk/USD, from upstream `release` (v26.08, ee47c679). The old usdGeospatial prototype branch is disregarded. | A stale `geospatial-crs` branch may still exist on the fork; Simon deletes it by hand. |
| D7 | **Everything in the fork**, no separate web repo. Upstreamable code and app code in separate directories and separate commits. | See commit rules in `CLAUDE.md`. |
| D8 | **No GitHub CI.** All builds and tests run locally on Simon's machine, so he can observe the devops complexity. | Upstream workflows only trigger on push to `dev`/`release` and PRs to `dev`; leave them untouched. |
| D9 | Primary platform **AlmaLinux 9** (same as Pixar's v26.08 test platform: Alma 9.5, GCC 11.5, CMake 3.30, Python 3.9). Workspace reproducible on macOS and Windows. Podman on Alma; `emscripten/emsdk:5.0.7` image is the reference wasm build. | |
| D10 | Tools: JetBrains (CLion for C++, WebStorm for the web app, PyCharm for the reference), Chrome DWARF extension for WASM debugging, Vite dev server or nginx in a container with COOP/COEP. | |
| D11 | No time estimates in the plan. | |
| D12 | wasm32 first; wasm64 only if memory runs out. | Settled 2026-11-21; peak memory is measured in C4. |
| D13 | **Global SceneView: anchors in EPSG:4979, render mapping in JS.** The scene index outputs each 3DOL as a geographic 3D anchor (lon, lat, ellipsoidal height) plus a Float64 matrix from mesh-local units to the anchor's ENU frame in metres. JS maps the anchor into render space in Float64 (since W1: the derivative of the SDK's geographic-to-render mapping, see `RECORDED_FORMAT.md`), splits off a float32-exact origin and composes the final matrix. Local SceneViews keep the view SR as output CRS, since that is their render space. | Decided 2026-11-21 after W0: global render space is ECEF on a 6378137 m sphere, not EPSG:4978, so C++ must not target it directly or reproduce the SDK's sphere mapping. W1 refined the JS side: `renderCoordinateTransformAt` is metric on the sphere and drifts from lon/lat-placed content by 0.1-0.3 %, so the frame comes from `toRenderCoordinates`. |
| D14 | **Schema name `GeospatialCRS`** for the typed CRS definition prim, as in the proposal's schema table and section headings (its USDA examples still say `CoordinateReferenceSystem`). C++ class `UsdGeospatialCRS` via the schema's `className`. Name kept in the tokens file. | Decided 2026-11-21. Ask the proposal authors which name is meant; a rename is cheap. |
| D15 | **Two Python venvs, both Python 3.12:** `<ws>/venv` for the native build (bindings, usdview, usdGenSchema) and `<ws>/venv-reference` for the offline reference (usd-core, pyproj, numpy). | Decided 2026-11-21. Both contain a `pxr` package from different USD builds; one venv would make the result depend on PYTHONPATH and could mix two USD builds in one process. The reference stays independent of our C++ build (option D). `geo.py` manages both (`VENV_PYTHON`). |
| D16 | **Imaging in `usdGeospatialImaging`.** The usdImaging adapter for `GeospatialCRSBindingAPI`, the placement scene index (a usdImaging scene index plugin) and the scene index observer live in a new library `pxr/usdImaging/usdGeospatialImaging` (hd, usdImaging, usdGeospatial), like `usdSkel` + `usdSkelImaging`. `usdGeospatial` stays free of Hydra; its placement gets a value-based entry point the scene index calls. | Decided 2026-11-21 at the start of C3: `pxr/usd` builds before `pxr/imaging`, so `usdGeospatial` cannot link `hd`. |
| D17 | **proj.db: compress now, trim at I2.** The browser module embeds the full proj.db (10.7 MB of the 30.7 MB `.wasm`). It is served precompressed (`.wasm.gz`, 7.2 MB; nginx `gzip_static`, the dev server likewise); trimming proj.db to the demo CRSs moves to I2 with the other size work (`-Oz`, wasm-opt). | Decided 2026-11-21 in C4. Trimming must keep every referenced datum, ellipsoid, operation and extent consistent; compression gives most of the benefit without that risk. Brotli would give 4.6 MB but needs an nginx module the stock image lacks. |
| D18 | **No grids natively for now.** Native PROJ stays without libtiff and grid files, so T3 (grid-only datum shift) and T4 (NAVD88) are reported unsupported natively as in the browser. Grids are a follow-on (libtiff, pinned grid downloads shared with the reference). | Decided 2026-11-21 at the start of I1 (was open since C1). The I1 exit criterion only covers cases both engines can do. |
| D19 | **The reference uses our PROJ.** pyproj (3.8.0) in `venv-reference` is built from source against the workspace's PROJ 9.9.0 (`deps/native`), so reference, native and browser share one PROJ version. | Decided 2026-11-21 at the start of I1. Was pyproj's bundled PROJ 9.8.1. |
| D20 | **I1 implements every browser case of the test plan:** new sites for T2 (Helmert), T3 (grid-only), T4 (NAVD88), T5 (1 km model), T8 (heading 90, time-sampled heading); T6 screen error; T9 browser vs native; T11 engine named in results. T10 is the WASM ctest run; the Esri half of T11 waits for E1. | Decided 2026-11-21. |
| D21 | **The app uses the live module by default** (`?data=live`); `?data=recorded` (reference export, or `&src=recorded-cpp`) and `?data=w0` remain. | Decided 2026-11-21. |
| D22 | **T3: place with the best usable operation, report what was skipped.** When better operations need grids the engine lacks (e.g. NADCON5 for NAD27 at Redlands), the engine places with the best usable equation-based one, reports its accuracy, and lists the skipped operations with the missing grids (`skippedOperations`). The test plan's T3 row changes from "unsupported" to "placed with reported, degraded accuracy". | Decided 2026-11-21 in I1: no EPSG datum is grid-only to WGS 84, so "unsupported" cannot occur under the C1 policy; matches the proposal (the engine chooses, and reports operation and accuracy). |
| D23 | **Vertical CRSs are supported, with grids.** Native PROJ and WASM PROJ get libtiff; the workspace pins the grids the tests and the first real data need: EGM96 (`us_nga_egm96_15.tif`, ArcGIS 3D object layers with `vcsWkid` 5773), NADCON5 CONUS and a NAVD88 geoid (T3, T4); EGM2008 (the proposal's default for 2D CRSs) natively only, for its size. The browser fetches each grid an operation needs on demand. Supersedes D18 and the "no grids in the browser" part of D5. | Decided 2026-11-21 after reading a real 3D object layer (Zurich office, WGS 84 + EGM96 heights): ignoring the vertical datum puts it about 48 m low. Implemented 2026-11-22. |
| D24 | **Adobe's glTF file format plugin, ported from the 3dtiles prototype**, lives in `third_party/adobe-usd-gltf` (Apache-2.0, not upstreamable to OpenUSD), built from the root CMakeLists behind an option, natively and for WASM; tinygltf is a pinned `geo.py` download. ArcGIS 3D object layers serve glb, not USD; wrapper layers reference the glb through it. | Decided 2026-11-21. Source: fork branch `3dtiles-prototype`, commits 55e91dc4c (port of adobe/USD-Fileformat-plugins main, 2025-12-07) and 87f26b314 (point geometry), on v25.11. |
| D25 | Display geoid correction: the app draws live anchors lowered by the EGM96 geoid height N at each anchor (module `geoidHeights`, EPSG:4979 to EPSG:4326+5773 through the engine, grid fetched on demand), because the SceneView draws heights as ellipsoidal and World Elevation's are orthometric (its service: "Heights are orthometric", no geoid named). On with terrain (`&geoid=1|0`). Placement, recorded data and scoring stay ellipsoidal (D13 unchanged). | Option 2 of three; outputting EGM96 heights from C++ would reopen D13 and change every expectation. EGM96 stands in for whatever geoid the terrain uses (EGM2008 differs by under a metre in Zurich). |
